questions.question: should I treat my boots out of box ? Annnnd how often should I treat them ?

hybrid.answer:
**Short answer:** It depends on the boot. He says not to treat pretreated, finished leather out of the box, but distressed or rustic leather is worth conditioning. After that, he says to treat when the leather looks or feels dry, not on a fixed schedule. His advice comes mostly from Blundstones, so it may not carry over to every boot.

**Out of the box**
- Reading Blundstone's FAQ, he notes that most Blundstones are pretreated, so he says not to treat them out of the box. Treating them again won't do much, since it just rolls off. [1]
- The exception is rustic brown, Crazy Horse brown and rustic black leathers. They are distressed and don't carry the same pretreatment as finished, oiled leather. [2]
- For his rustic pair, he recommends conditioning "100%". He doesn't recommend leaving them dry, even though they look cool that way, if you want them to last. [3]
- Treating will darken the leather. [2]
- In his first review he also said he'd recommend the boots if you will keep them treated. Treatment is why they're water resistant out of the box. [4]
- He later corrected his early belief that his distressed pair was already treated. [5]

**How often (newest view first)**
- **2022:** He says he doesn't have a set answer and expects flak either way. He personally probably does too little and treats "when I feel like they need it". Many people are more regimented, and it depends on how much you wear them and where. [6]
- His signs it's time: the leather looks or feels dry, or water isn't beading on top. Dry means more wax or oil. He also says to clean boots regularly, because dirt wears the leather down faster. [7]
- His order is always clean, condition, then wax. [8]
- **2019:** He said you may have to wax them every month, or maybe every week if you're hard on them. [4] He also said to condition any leather you haven't treated in a few months. [9]

He hasn't given a specific schedule for boots other than Blundstones in the videos available here.

questions.question: So if I buy the levis 501 shrink to fit will they get tighter after washing?

hybrid.answer:
Yes, the first soak and dry is what shrinks them, so they get noticeably tighter then, especially in the waist. He doesn't say what later regular washes do in the videos available here, but his advice is to keep the heat and the dryer away.

**His most recent view (2025):** He likes the 501 STF because it's shrink-to-fit. You put it in the bathtub and it shrinks, and he says you should usually go two sizes up [1].

**Washing and drying (2023):** He says a dryer would make the jeans a lot smaller from the start [2]. His advice is not to toss STFs in the dryer or rinse them in very hot water, and then you can get a really nice fit [3]. He also bets that with frequent wear they stretch out to about the size of regular rinsed 501s [4].

**What the tightness is like (2021 and 2019):**
- In 2021 he says that after they shrink he usually has to pull them on really hard and they're really tight in the waist. He suggests a tub soak to ease that [5].
- In 2019, after his own shrink, the jeans slimmed up mainly in the waist [6]. A week later the waist and upper thigh had stretched enough that he could wear a belt [7].

**Sizing to plan for it:** In 2021 he says to size up two in the waist and two inches in length, and the pants will then fit regularly after you get them wet [8].

questions.question: I'm usually a 33x30 in Levi's 502s, what size should I buy in these? [501 STF]

hybrid.answer:
By his rule, buy a **35 waist x 32 length** in the 501 STF, though he hasn't said how 502 sizing compares.

**His rule (most recent first)**
- In 2025 he says you should usually go two sizes up in the shrink-to-fit 501 [1].
- In 2021 he says Levi's advice is correct: size up two in the waist and add one length, which is two inches more. After that, he says, the pants fit regularly once wet [2]. Applied to your 33x30, that is 35x32.
- In 2023 he notes that STF waist sizes aren't vanity sized. He went up two sizes, which is why you size up two in Levi's, since they shrink down [3].

**His own experience**
- He bought a 29 waist x 30 length and could barely pull them on at first. He says he's glad he did, since the waist is a good fit now, but he would have gotten a 32 length [4].
- In his first 2019 video, he ignored Levi's advice to go up one or two sizes in the waist and added length. He says jeans are usually too long on him [5]. The later videos suggest he came around to Levi's advice.

**Caveats**
- He warns that the size you'd need may not exist. He says that for a 34 you'd go to a 36, though he doesn't think a 36 exists [2]. Odd sizes like a 35 may not be offered, and he doesn't say what to do in that case.
- He hasn't covered Levi's 502s or how they compare to the 501 in the videos available here, so his rule is applied to your stated size only.

questions.question: Why do you cuff your jeans?

hybrid.answer:
He cuffs mainly because of the look he's going for. Wider, straight-leg jeans don't suit his style uncuffed, and jeans that run too long look bad to him.

**Most recent (2020):** On his Levi's 501 STF, he says he would have bought a 32 length, but he cuffed them anyway because he doesn't think his current style "lends itself to not cuffed wider legged pants" [1].

**Earlier (2019), on length and width:** When trying the unshrunk 501s, he says it's "all about length" for him. If jeans look too long they "just look bad," and he says that's the first thing he looks at [2]. He found the wide 501s looked better with a cuff or a pin roll, though still wider than he likes. He also said a cuff shouldn't be too thick [2].

**A nuance on boots:** In his L.L. Bean boot video he says he used to always cuff his jeans but now likes them worn down over his boots more [3]. That is about boots, though. He doesn't say he has given up cuffing in general, and in the 2020 video he was still cuffing his 501s [1].

questions.question: So do you prefer [the Red Wing 3335s] over the 1907s?

hybrid.answer:
Yes, he prefers the 3335s over the 1907s, at least as of his 2022 video, where he calls them his favorite boots he's ever had. His 2023 video adds a wrinkle: he's selling them.

**Most recent (Sept 2023):** He says he's on record calling the 3335s his favorite Red Wings of all time and that they "still might be". He likes them for their stitch-down construction, lighter weight and nimbler feel, and says they're easier for walking or a light hike. He still lists the 1907s, 875s and Iron Rangers as having characteristics he really likes. Even so, the 3335s are on his sell list as he cuts down his collection [1].

**Oct 2022 (the 3335 review):** He says they beat his Blundstones, the 1907s and the 875s. His reasoning is that he's going for hikes and walks in the woods rather than doing heritage work. He calls the 3335s a dramatically better all-around boot [2]. He also likes their Vibram mini lug sole, which he thinks won't break down as fast as the crepe soles on the 875s and 1907s [3].

**The caveat:** The 1907s and 875s are more beefily constructed, so for a tough work boot he says the 3335s probably aren't the ones to go for [2]. On waterproofing, he doesn't think stitch-down gives the 3335s a big edge over Goodyear-welted boots, and says the 3335s' single stitch limits the advantage [4]. In his earlier 1907 video (2021), he praised the 1907 as the best Red Wing moc toe, for its storm welt, removable leather footbed and leather laces for about $10 more than the 875 [5].

questions.question: How do you feel bout blunnies as of Late 2023?

hybrid.answer:
As of the most recent video (September 2023), The Iron Snail is still a big fan of Blundstones, even though he's retiring some of his pairs.

**His latest view (Sept 2023)**
- He says the 585s, the boots from his first-ever video, have been worn constantly and have held up. They remain "probably my most water resistant boots" and he calls Blundstones "just incredible" and says he's always loved them [1].
- He notes some people seem not to like them [1].
- He is still retiring those 585s, saying it's time, as part of cutting down his boot collection [1].
- He treats Blundstones as slip-on shoes he can "flop on" quickly, whatever the weather, and says he's keeping that kind of pair, though it could easily go on the sell list [2].
- The heavy-duty Blundstone work boots (the Extremes) are also going. He describes them as steel toe, fire and electrical hazard resistant, and very water resistant nubuck, not waterproof as he had thought [3].

**Earlier view (2019)**
- In his first review he recommended the Blundstones "100%" as long as you're going to treat them, and he called them by far his favourites of the boots he owned then [4][5].
- He warned that their water resistance depends on the treatment, so they need to be kept treated [5].

His opinion has held steady over time. He still likes the boots and says the 585s have lasted well, and he is letting some pairs go to make room.

questions.question: How does the made in England boot stack up to Solovairs? [Dr. Martens]

hybrid.answer:
In his 2022 Dr. Martens video, The Iron Snail says Solovair is the better buy: it is cheaper than Made in England Docs and better built, and he thinks the leather and midsoles are about equal. He has not compared the two directly since.

**Where he thinks they're equal**
- He says the Made in England leather will age fine and is probably on par with Solovair [1]. He says the same about the midsoles [2].

**Where he thinks Solovair wins**
- **Price:** he says Solovairs are actually cheaper than Made in England Docs [3]. He thinks much of the extra cost of the England version is simply the "made in England" part [4].
- **Comfort:** Solovair boots have a shank [5], which he says makes them a bit more comfortable over long periods [6].
- **Resoling:** he says they're Goodyear welted in a more regularly accepted way, so they're easier to resole [7].
- **Overall:** he sums it up as "cheaper better quality better features" [8]. He says the 8-eye derby is essentially the exact same boot as the Dr. Martens [8].

**Caveats**
- The only thing Solovair doesn't do is the yellow stitching. If that matters to you, he says you have to get the Made in England Docs for the highest quality [9].
- His own Solovair pair had problems. A back tab ripped off and a lace snapped, though he assumed this was a manufacturing defect [10].

**Newer video (2023)**
His later Made in England vs. Thailand comparison doesn't mention Solovair. In it, he says the $90 premium for the England boots is probably not worth it on a purely practical basis [11]. He adds that you'd have to be a mega fan to get them [12].

questions.question: Hi, I am going on a 4 day hike and I am wondering if I can use my blundstone for them, what do you think?

hybrid.answer:
He hasn't covered multi-day hiking in Blundstones, so he gives no direct verdict on a 4-day hike. What he does say suggests caution.

**Ankle support:** After about a year of wear, he says Blundstones are "not good boots for mountaining apparently" because they lack good ankle support [1]. He still took his pair up and down a few mountains in Maine, and says they scuffed a little but held up well [2].

**Water:** He's positive about water resistance for short exposure. After a year untreated, he says they're fine if you're crossing a brook or a stream, or standing in mud for a bit [3]. He wouldn't stand in water for hours [4]. They are water resistant, not waterproof, so don't expect them to cope with long soakings.

**Care:** He says to buy them knowing you'll have to look after them, since the water resistance comes from treatment that needs keeping up [5]. He later corrected himself: Blundstone's FAQ says the rustic brown leathers aren't pretreated like finished, oiled ones [6]. If yours is a distressed style, he'd condition it before a long trip. He also says he'd choose a smoother leather over the rustic nubuck [7].

**Fit over time:** After a year, the elastics had loosened a little but were still tight enough to keep the boot on [8].

Taken together, his experience is of day hikes and mountain climbs where they held up. He never describes carrying a pack for several days in them. If you go ahead, his points are the lack of ankle support, the need to keep the leather treated, and limiting how long you stand in water.

questions.question: I'm 5'11-225 lbs with a dad bod. What's the most cost efficient and quality t shirt for me? Also, what size would u prefer?

hybrid.answer:
For your build, he'd most likely point you to **Muji** as the cost-efficient pick. He hasn't given a size for someone of your height and weight, so the sizing advice below is his general rules applied to you.

**Top pick: Muji (his most recent view, Sept 2025)**
- He calls the roughly $20 Uniqlo "probably the best t-shirt that you can get bar none for the price" [1]. But he says that if you're taller or wider, you'd want Muji [2].
- Muji costs about $4 or $5 more, but it's "significantly longer and a good deal wider" [2]. He adds that you'd probably like it "if you're a little bigger" [2].
- In June 2025 he said the extra ~$10 over Uniqlo felt justified, because the shirt feels better and has a thicker, tighter collar [3].

**Other value options**
- **Uniqlo:** He wears it all the time and says the bound collar keeps the neck from wiggling [4]. In 2024 he gave the heavyweight crew neck his best value heavyweight/all-around award [5].
- **Kirkland (Costco six-pack, ~$25):** He calls it quite long and can't recommend it enough for a shirt under $5-6 [6][7]. His shrink test showed 4% in width and 2% in length [7].
- **House of Blanks ($35):** He calls this combed ring-spun shirt, made in Canada, an outstanding value [8].
- **Los Angeles Apparel:** He thinks it might win if you size down one [9].
- **Bronson ($29) and Bravestar ($32):** He had them neck and neck for greatest value in that video [10].

**Size**
He hasn't said which size he'd choose for 5'11" and 225 lb. The closest thing is his rule that taller or wider guys should pick Muji over Uniqlo for the extra length and width [2]. On his own preferences, he likes a lot of space across the shoulders [11]. His only size advice for a specific shirt in these videos was to size down one in the Los Angeles Apparel tee [9].

questions.question: Am I the only one who loves these videos but in the end still has no idea which to buy? Please just tell me: buy this one, or these 3. I can't decide between 25 options. [t-shirts]

hybrid.answer:
You're not alone, and he doesn't name one overall winner. He says the best tee depends on your preferences, so he only picks a favorite in each category [1]. If you want a shortlist, these are his picks:

- **All-arounders:** J Press x American Trench. He's torn between it and 3Sixteen, but goes with J Press for its rougher hand feel [2].
- **Japanese tees:** Wonder Looper. He says it has a much better, more universal fit than Samurai [3].
- **Supremes (his favorite category):** Merz b. Schwanen edges out Lady White for him that day [3].
- **Best value:** Front General Store is his pick today, though he says he might choose House of Blanks tomorrow [4]. For a budget starter tee, he calls the $20 Uniqlo probably the best you can get for the price [5][6].
- **Heavyweights:** American Giant Everest wins that category by a long shot [3]. He also says it is far too heavy for most people [7], so skip it unless you want a really heavy tee.

**How to narrow it down:** his own dividing line is texture. If you like character and a rougher feel, he points to J Press or Front General Store. If you want perfectly smooth with no torque, he points to 3Sixteen or House of Blanks [2][4].

questions.question: Do you have any particular favorites for more athletic builds? I sometimes have trouble with high quality tees being tight on the shoulders and boxy around the waist

hybrid.answer:
He doesn't name a tee for athletic builds in the videos available here, but a few comments come close.

**Closest match: Asket.** He says it's what he imagines "very jacked or slim men" wearing at coffee shops, because it flows and feels like glass [1]. It didn't make his final list only because that list was for shirts under $50 [1]. His picks in the Supremes category (MSB, Asket, Lady White, Knickerbocker) are all clean, elevated minimalist tees, and he gave that category's win to Merz b. Schwanen. He likes its fit across the neck and chest, which he calls unique and very distinctive [2].

**Shoulder room.** He likes a lot of space across the shoulders and praises the J. Press x American Trench fit [3]. That was his pick in the all-arounders category [4]. He didn't say how it fits through the waist.

**Fit that suits many people.** He chose Wonder Looper in the Japanese category because it has a much better, more universal fit than Samurai [5]. He describes Samurai as cropped and wide, so it may not suit everyone [5].

**Not covered.** He didn't test or compare tees for shoulder tightness or boxy waists, so he gives no direct advice on that combination.

questions.question: 1907 vs the 875's? What's the difference?

hybrid.answer:
**Short version:** he thinks the 1907 is the better buy for a Red Wing moc toe, mainly because of its storm welt and the extras it comes with. The 875 is a Goodyear-welted boot that costs about $10 less.

**Welt construction**
- The 875 is Goodyear welted. He calls Goodyear welts "incredible", durable and pretty water resistant [1].
- The 1907 has a storm (Norwegian-like) welt, which to him is "invaluable" [2].
- He notes that, per the popular view he's seen on Reddit, Red Wing's storm welt is just another strip of leather stitched onto the welt. He says he isn't quite sure about this [3].

**Price and what you get**
- The 1907 is about $10 more than the 875 [4].
- For that, he says you get a removable leather footbed, which he says typically costs about $40 separately, plus the storm welt and free leather laces [5][2]. He argues it's effectively the better deal.
- The removable footbeds can also be pulled out at the end of the day so the boots dry faster [5].

**Soles**
- In his later video (Oct 2022), he says both the 875 and 1907 have crepe soles that he thinks break down faster than the Vibram mini lug sole on the 3335 [6]. In the earlier 1907 video he also says he doesn't really like the crepe soles [7].

**His verdict, and how it changed**
- In 2021 he says the 1907 is Red Wing's best heritage boot "by far" and recommends it if you're looking at a moc toe Red Wing [7].
- By the 2022 video, his favourite Red Wings are the 3335s rather than the 1907s or 875s [8].

**Water performance**
- In his water test, the 1907's right boot leaked almost immediately through the stitching while the left stayed dry. He still thinks they'd hold up fine in rain, grass or mud [9].
- He hasn't run a comparable water test on the 875 in the videos available here.

questions.question: How does Uniqlo compare to The Front General Store,  Proclub, and Hanes? ie what is the best budget shirt?

hybrid.answer:
**Short answer:** Of these four, he leans toward Uniqlo as the best budget shirt on price-to-quality. His latest word is that the $20 Uniqlo is "probably the best t-shirt that you can get bar none for the price" [1]. Front General Store is the nicer shirt, but it costs about twice as much. He never ranks Uniqlo directly against Pro Club or Hanes, so those comparisons are pieced together from separate videos.

**Uniqlo (newest view, Sept 2025):** He calls it your "starter t-shirt". It's open-ended and a bit rough, and if you're taller or wider he'd point you to Muji instead [2]. In June 2025 he said the bound neck collar keeps it from wiggling, and that for $15 the price-to-quality ratio is so good "you could end the video here" [3]. Back in 2024 he named the heavyweight Uniqlo crew neck a contender for best bargain tee, with a bound, ribbed collar [4]. Its shrink tests were about 2.3–2.5% in width and 2% in length [5]. In June 2025 he put Bronson and Bravestar slightly above Uniqlo on value [6].

**Front General Store:** This is the step-up pick. In 2025 he described it as a $40, 100% Japan-made shirt with great proportions and great feel, and a previous winner [7]. In 2024 he called it one of the best shirts you could get if you want a Japanese-made upgrade without spending over $40 [8]. He gave it a 6/10 for softness and measured 1.2% shrink in width and 0% in length, since it's pre-washed [8].

**Pro Club:** He liked it. He calls it an old-school American shirt, but also the roughest on that list [9]. He gave it a 4/10 for softness and measured 2.78% shrink in width and 6.86% in length [10]. That length shrink is much higher than Uniqlo's.

**Hanes:** He calls it a classic $10 great shirt, much softer than Pro Club [11][12]. He gave it a 7/10 for softness, with 1.45% shrink in width and 6.73% in length [12]. So it's the cheapest of the group, but it shrinks noticeably in length.

**Overall lean:** Uniqlo is the best all-round budget shirt, thanks to its bound collar, low price and comparatively small shrink. Front General Store is worth the extra money if you want Japanese-made quality. Hanes and Pro Club are cheap, decent shirts, but they shrink more in length.

questions.question: Would you recommend this or the flint and tinder for someone who would use it like a rain jacket but also a windbreaker and a spring light jacket?

hybrid.answer:
**Short answer:** I'm assuming "this" means the Barbour, since that's the jacket he ranked #1. If so, he leans Barbour for your use. He hasn't directly compared the two for rain, wind and spring use, and he never calls either one a windbreaker.

**Barbour**
- In his 2025 ranking it was the top pick with 186 votes, and he says that's why Barbour "crushed the competition" [1].
- He stresses it isn't a dedicated rain jacket, but a lightweight 6 oz Sylkoil that you can wear over layers in any season, including spring [2].
- It has rain-focused features: a throat latch, snaps for a hood and storm cuffs, which he calls helpful in inclement weather [3]. In his 2021 review he also says to get the snap-on hood [4].
- Rain performance depends on the wax. He says a freshly waxed Bedale didn't leak in a shower test, but it isn't waterproof, only very water-resistant when properly treated [5]. As the patina develops you lose a little practicality [6].
- He ties extra wind and water resistance to thornproof, the tighter combed-and-calendered cotton [7]. The 2025 jacket he showed is Sylkoil, so that extra isn't something he claims for it.

**Flint and Tinder (Huckberry Waxed Trucker)**
- He says it's built for everyone [8]. It's lighter weight but "not crazy lightweight", and it's lined, so you don't get wax on your skin [9].
- He says it's hard not to recommend, mainly because of the price: $300 for a lined, US-made jacket in Martexin fabric [10].
- That segment was sponsored by Huckberry, though he says he'd praised the jacket many times before the sponsorship [11].
- In 2023 he described the Huckberry trucker as lighter-weight and without a lining. He said it suits a regular guy who wears it in the rain with a hat [12][13]. He didn't mention whether it's the same version as the lined one in 2025.
- He doesn't mention a hood or storm cuffs on it in these videos.

**Bottom line:** For rain use, the Barbour's storm details and hood option give it the edge in what he's said. The Flint and Tinder is the easier, cheaper all-round pick. For wind and spring, he praises the Barbour's layering flexibility and the Flint and Tinder's comfort, but he doesn't rank them against each other.

questions.question: Great video. But just curious, how can you say it's a con that the Huckberry jacket is unlined when they sell two different versions of lined waxed truckers: wool, and flannel?

hybrid.answer:
His con was specific to the unlined Huckberry jacket he reviewed in 2023, not to every Huckberry waxed trucker. In his newer video he says the Flint and Tinder Waxed Trucker is lined.

**2023 (the con):** He called the Huckberry wax trucker he reviewed the "cheapest most simple unlined basic jacket" in his lineup [1]. He said the con for it and the Rogue Territory jacket is that they aren't lined. He personally always likes a lining on waxed jackets so the wax isn't touching your clothes or arms [2].

**2025 (the lined version):** In a video sponsored by Huckberry [3], he says the Flint and Tinder Waxed Trucker is lined, so it's comfortable and you don't get wax on your skin. He also mentions a wool-lined version that he hasn't tried yet, which he says is heavier overall [4]. He doesn't mention a flannel-lined version in the videos available here.

**His softening on lining:** In the same 2025 video, he says that in his old age he sees why someone wouldn't line a jacket. He notes that satin-lined sleeves can stick to your skin once it's a little warm [5].

So the con was about the specific unlined jacket he tested, and he hasn't said lined versions share it.

questions.question: Do you know how these fit compared to the 875s? [Red Wing 3335s]

hybrid.answer:
He hasn't directly compared the fit of the 3335s to the 875s in the videos available here, but he does describe how the 3335s fit.

**3335 fit (2022):** He went true to size and says they fit fine, and he calls sizing "pretty straightforward with Red Wings" [1]. He adds that the boots have a slim profile and taper down. With thin cotton socks in warm weather he had no tightness, but with wool socks his toes felt squished and he couldn't wiggle them much [1].

**Red Wing sizing in general (2021):** In his 1907 video, he usually wears an 8 in boots, bought an 8 in Red Wings, and says they fit perfect [2]. He says leather boots should fit snug but not squished, since the leather will mold to your feet [3]. That video covers the 1907, not the 875, so it is not an 875 fit verdict.

**What he did compare:** He says the 1907s and 875s are more beefily constructed than the 3335s [4]. That is about build, not fit.

**Bottom line:** His advice is to go true to size on the 3335s, but expect a narrower, tapered toe area, especially with thick socks. He hasn't said how the 875s' toe room compares.
